PLAN YOUR REQUIREMENT

A useful brief.
A clearer next step.

Prototypes, low-volume products, OEM components and complete mechanical assemblies.

Decisions to make early

Define whether the next milestone is a functional prototype, design validation or a production batch. Identify unresolved design choices before estimating the production route.

What to agree before work begins

Agree the product definition, bill of materials where available, approval sample requirements, quantity and acceptance criteria.

BEFORE YOU ENQUIRE

Questions,
answered.

Can a project begin with a prototype?+

Include the purpose of the prototype and what you need to learn from it, such as fit, assembly or usability. The prototype scope and its relationship to a later production version are agreed separately.

What changes between a prototype and a batch?+

Materials, tooling, assembly methods and inspection plans may need review. Confirm the approved revision and any changes before treating a prototype as a production reference.

A CLEAR START

What to share.

Product brief, drawings, target quantities and delivery requirements.

Technical scope, material suitability, tolerances, inspection criteria, pricing and timing are confirmed after reviewing your requirements.

A CONNECTED APPROACH

Think beyond
one process.

Your project may need design, fabrication, finishing and assembly together. Include the complete requirement so each step can be considered in context.
